claim: Schueth's 2025 paper (arXiv:2511.22255), in its own literature review, states that Ucar's thesis obtained explicit formulas for ALL b_l(C), l>=0, for orbifold cone points at constant curvature, expressed as b_l(C) = kappa^l * (1/n) * p_l(n) where p_l is a polynomial of degree 2l+2 -- independently confirming (outside the manuscript under review) that these formulas are explicit, not merely degree-bounded.
stance_target: The manuscript's planned K<=n+1 extension requires new cone-coefficient computation for l=2,3
scope_conditions: Two-dimensional orbifold cone point, constant curvature kappa in R
quoted_support: Ucar [13] obtained explicit formulas for all b_l(C) for cone points C of two-dimensional orbifolds under the special assumption that the orbifold has constant curvature kappa in R... b_l(C) can then be written as kappa^l times 1/n p_l(n), where p_l is a certain polynomial of order 2l+2.

claim: Schueth's 2025 paper self-cites her own 2019 Ann. Inst. Fourier paper as the source of the b_2(C) formula for orbifold cone points, describing it as 'a linear combination of K(p)^2 and (Delta K)(p), where the coefficients are, again, rational functions of the order of the cone point.'
stance_target: b_2 for orbifold cone points at constant curvature is already established (Schueth 2019, Theorem 4.1)
scope_conditions: Orbifold cone point, general (possibly non-constant) curvature
quoted_support: In [10], the author obtained a similar formula for b_2(C) in the same context; b_2(C) turns out to be a linear combination of K(p)^2 and (Delta K)(p), where the coefficients are, again, rational functions of the order of the cone point.

claim: Schueth's 2025 paper studies a strictly more general singularity class than orbifold cone points -- rotationally symmetric but not-necessarily-flat conic singularities where half-integer powers t^{j/2} and log t terms appear in the heat trace, absent in the orbifold case -- and its main new coefficient b_{1/2}(C) is not directly usable for the manuscript's constant-curvature orbifold setting.
stance_target: Relevance scope of Schueth 2025 to the manuscript's constant-curvature orbifold cone coefficients
scope_conditions: General 2D conic singularity, rotationally invariant metric, K(p) may be unbounded approaching the cone point
quoted_support: This is a sharp contrast to the behavior of b_0(C) and of those coefficients b_j(C) which appear in certain known formulas in the case of orbifold cone points or corners of geodesic polygons.

J.'), with identical volume/year/pages 56 (2008) 205-238 across all variants.
stance_target: Bibliographic consistency of the DGGW citation across sources
quoted_support: E.B. Dryden, C.S. Gordon, S.J. Greenwald, and D.L. Webb, Asymptotic expansion of the heat kernel for orbifolds, Michigan J. Math. 56 (2008), no. 1, 205-238.
